summary.text: 忘 means “forget.” It is analyzed as 心 “heart/mind” combined with 亡 as a sound component, linking forgetting with the mind and giving a pronunciation cue.

formation.text: A phonosemantic compound: 心 contributes the meaning category “heart/mind,” while 亡 supplies a sound cue. This analysis is recorded in the Han lexicographic tradition and in accounts of bronze and later forms; it does not establish when the graph was first formed.

components.text: 心 contributes the heart or mind meaning category. The evidence does not show that it depicts a separate scene within 忘.
亡 is the phonetic element in this graph, as described in the Han analysis and the account of bronze and later forms.

sound.text: In Baxter–Sagart 2014, 亡 is *maŋ and 忘 has *maŋ and *maŋ-s; their Middle Chinese forms are mjang and mjang / mjangH. The comparison supports a sound relationship in that reconstruction system, but does not date the compound or establish a particular sound change.

history.text: A paleographic summary lists 忘 in a late Spring-and-Autumn bronze inscription and Warring States, seal, clerical, and regular-script forms, and analyzes the graph as 心 plus 亡. This listing does not establish the earliest occurrence; no securely dated oracle-bone example was verified.
The curated seal-script-style image illustrates the received 心-and-亡 analysis. It is a modern digital redraw, not an artifact photograph, and does not establish an earlier form or date.

uncertainties.text: No securely dated oracle-bone occurrence or Shang-era attestation was verified, and the listed later forms do not establish when the graph first appeared.
The proposed account that 忘 derives from 亡 with a perfective suffix is unverified here; the evidence does not establish that word-history account or a separate borrowing of the whole graph.

Current Mandarin readings 亡 wáng and 忘 wàng do not establish an ancient sound relation. The historical reconstruction comparison supports a sound comparison but does not prove a particular sound change or date of formation.

senses.gloss: not to recognize or know; forget
senses.period: Han lexicographic tradition; earliest attestation dating unresolved
senses.text: The Han lexicographic gloss is 不識也, “not to recognize or know.” The evidence does not establish this as the graph’s earliest attested use.
Current reference material includes “neglect,” “miss,” and “omit” alongside “forget,” but provides no dated sequence or evidence that these senses developed in that order.

limitations.text: No dated early textual uses or ordered development among “forget,” “neglect,” “miss,” and “omit” were established. The historical and current glosses do not by themselves establish that chronology.

overview.text: 忘 means “forget.” 心 points to the heart or mind, while 亡 provides a sound cue; together they form a compound associated with forgetting.

components.text: 心 connects the character’s meaning with the heart or mind.
亡 provides a sound cue; historical reconstructions show a closer match than the different modern Mandarin readings.

relationships.text: 心 contributes the heart/mind meaning category in the recorded analysis of 忘.
亡 serves as the sound component in the recorded analysis of 忘; the cited Baxter–Sagart reconstructions compare 亡 *maŋ with 忘 *maŋ and *maŋ-s.
